body:
What Wind Can Do: 1. Air that moves (moving air). 2. You can feel it on your face, and you can see what it moves. 3. Bend tall trees (also push kites and sailboats). 4. Drawing shows something the wind is moving, such as a kite, leaves, a flag or a sailboat.
Wind Hunt: the drawing shows something the wind really moved outside (leaves, grass, a flag, hair, clothes, a streamer), and the student tells what it was and whether the wind was gentle or strong.
Wind Walk Count: 1. 5 leaves. 2. 2 flags. 3. The leaves. 4. The kite (1 kite). 5. 8 things.
Wind Check: 1. Moving air. 2. No, we cannot see it; we know it is there because we feel it and see what it moves. 3. The strong wind. 4. Any thing wind pushes: leaves, a kite, a flag, a sailboat, a pinwheel, clouds. 5. Drawing shows something being moved by the wind (bent trees, flying leaves, a kite).
Scoring tip: on "I can tell what wind is", a student who says "it blows things" is Getting there; "air that moves" is Got it! When counting, a student who counts all 8 correctly but mixes up which group is biggest is Got it! on counting and Getting there on comparing.
title: Answer key: Wind on the Move
